steps.content: [CG Montage: Main storyline featuring battlefield scenes, Jasmine, antagonist Adelaide, Hella, and the Black Ring]
Blood...
Do you smell it? The scent of steel and blood...
The sound of bones breaking... how melodious...
Bite through them... Tear them apart. Don't hold back... You should have done this long ago.
Kill them, kill them!
[Red Flash Back to Reality]
Your vision blurs as your legs give way, dropping you to your knees. Your body is no longer your own to command.

The shackles are ready to crumble at the slightest pressure, their integrity compromised by the new Black Ring. Fresh contamination from the Sinner behind you—the one wielding a Rancor—sears through your mind like acid. This agony is a burden you willingly chose to share with her.

You try to steady your breath, but your grip on the crank slips as the last of your strength bleeds away. The navigation beacon flickers, growing dim; both the battery pack and your body are running on fumes.
Ceto notices your faltering state immediately, her own movements visibly slowing in response.
Just focus on the fight. I'll be fine... The fleet still needs the beacon to guide them. We've come too far to fail now. I'm not falling here.

You grit your teeth, forcing yourself to crank the generator for another surge of power, a pathetic attempt to prove your resilience. But you feel it clearly now: through the connection of the shackles, the Rancor's madness is gently, inexorably pulling your consciousness into its depths.

Ceto knows precisely what you're enduring, the same whispers that have been her constant companions for years. She also knows you will never speak of this pain, just as you've hidden your exhaustion and failing sight.
[Staircase]
Could you help me carry the lens up there? And don't look at me like that. I'm perfectly fine and bursting with energy after the meal.

That ${PlayerName}, who could barely walk a straight line, clutched the hard-won toolbox as he staggered toward the lantern room. He was determined to repair the navigation beacon before the thunderstorm broke.
steps.female_content: That ${PlayerName}, who could barely walk a straight line, clutched the hard-won toolbox as she staggered toward the lantern room. She was determined to repair the navigation beacon before the thunderstorm broke.

steps.content: She should have noticed it sooner. Temporary blindness had been a mercy. Keep pushing like this, this DisCity native's fragile physique would likely face far worse consequences. Dehydration? Collapse? Being torn apart like the other lighthouse keepers? She couldn't bear to imagine further.
Ceto, you know what I thought when I went blind in the Black Tide?
The fragile figure in her eyes paused on the stairs, turning back breathlessly:
I thought... it was so dark. An emptiness with nothing in front of you. No direction, no guide, nothing to hold onto. But that also meant...
No obstacles.
Since I knew there was nothing but the Black Tide and those monsters behind me, all I could do was swim forward. Faster. Just leave the shadows behind. There had to be land ahead. Somewhere.
Ceto despised such optimism, empty words that wouldn't fill a stomach or stop a monster. She looked up, scowling, yet her eyes fixed on the figure still pressing upward.

Those frail limbs—useless in a fight against the Tide Crawlers—clung to the rusted toolbox, carrying a weight she couldn't comprehend. Step by stubborn step, this person climbed toward what looked like an impossible hope.
So damn foolish... she thought, but swallowed the words. She had seen this kind of fool before. Watched them fall, one after another, only for new ones to rise and take their place.
Forward... tomorrow... land...
[Red Flash] [Knife Stabbing Sound]
Without a moment's hesitation, she drives the dagger into her own left shoulder.
What are you—
Simultaneously, the pressure crushing your mind eases significantly. Ceto is using pain to claw back her lucidity, deliberately lightening the burden of the Rancor that she shares with you.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Keep going!
She offers no further explanation, flicks the blood from her blade, and throws herself back into the fray.
You do get a brief moment to catch your breath. But the very next second—
—BOOM!!!

The barricaded metal plates blast inward. Shattered railings tear apart, spraying debris and rain in all directions. Several monsters surge onto the platform at once, an endless tide swarming behind them.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Just a little longer. The tide will fall soon.

Her voice trembles slightly from blood loss, but her grip on the knife is unshakable. You stand back-to-back in a circle of light barely two meters wide, with the abyss yawning below and a sea of Corruptors closing in.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Our bet isn't over yet!
She smothers her agony, forces back the encroaching contamination with a sweeping slash, and plants herself as the final barrier between you and the horde.
